key_insight: Whole-brain MRI deep learning showed modest HER2 prediction performance, with ROC-AUC increasing from 0.667 to 0.692 when expert tumour masks were added.
clinical_relevance: This exploratory approach could support future non-invasive HER2 assessment in breast cancer brain metastases but is not established for clinical decision-making.
method: Analysed post-contrast T1-weighted brain MRI from the public BCBM-Radiogenomics dataset.
Compared conventional radiomics with a simple fully convolutional network.
Tested the network with MRI alone and with an additional expert-derived tumour mask.
evidence_signal: Among 135 patients (70 HER2-positive, 65 HER2-negative), ROC-AUC was 0.602 for radiomics, 0.667 for MRI-only deep learning, and 0.692 for mask-guided deep learning.
watch_item: Modest performance and overlapping confidence intervals leave the benefit of tumour masks uncertain; broader validation is needed.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of HER2 Status from Whole-Brain MRI in Breast Cancer Brain Metastases
